subject: crowded city
title: What If Nobody Ever Died Again? Earth Gains an Italy Every Year

scenes.text: What if, from tonight, nobody on Earth ever died again? Within a year, you'd notice the extra Italy.
Right now about 170,000 people die every day, roughly 60 million a year. Tonight, that drops to zero.
Births don't stop: about 130 million a year. So the world grows by 130 million a year instead of 70. An extra billion every eight years.
By 2100, at today's birth rate, roughly 18 billion people. The UN expected us to peak at 10.3 billion and shrink.
Farming already takes half of Earth's habitable land to feed 8 billion. Feeding twice that, at today's yields, leaves nothing, even clearing every forest.
And it never levels off. The only brake left is having fewer children. Death, it turns out, is what makes room for the next person.

description:
What if nobody ever died again? About 60 million people die each year worldwide, roughly 170,000 a day, while about 130 million are born. Remove deaths and the world gains about 130 million people a year instead of 70 million, an extra billion every eight years, reaching roughly 18 billion by 2100 at today's birth rate, against the UN's projected peak of 10.3 billion in the 2080s.
Agriculture already uses about half of the planet's habitable land to feed 8 billion people, so more than doubling the population would outrun the land available, and with no deaths the growth would never stop on its own.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: About 117 billion humans have ever been born, so if nobody had ever died, Earth would already hold 14 times its current population. Would you want to live forever on a planet like that?
